subject: floatingIslandDiorama
pitch:
Category: Diorama.
Subject: floating sky island with ruins, waterfall and trees.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm planning a single static module for a floating sky island in Genshin-style teal/cream/gold palette with cel shading—rocky cone underside, grassy top, ruined pillars and an arch, a waterfall, trees, and glowing crystals. I need to figure out how the floating geometry should sit relative to y=0 given it's meant to hover rather than rest on the ground.

Drafting lathe outline points for the island's rocky cone and a separate overhanging grass-cap lathe near the rim, working out radii and heights so the grass edge overlaps the rock surface naturally.

Now I'm thinking through additional details: scattered downward-pointing cones under the island to suggest hanging stalactites, and a waterfall emerging from an edge point, built as a thin glowing stream of boxes falling to just above y=0 with mist spheres below, plus a small pond cylinder sitting on top of the island.

I'm refining the waypoints for the water stream path so it hugs the rock surface, checking the slope offsets at each segment, then deciding on a swept box or circular cross-section to give the stream some thickness along its path.

Now I'm designing the ruins: a hexagonal stone platform with ring of six pillars of varying heights (some broken), gold trim bands, and a back arch made from two taller pillars plus a lintel bearing a glowing rune emblem, with a floating crystal orb nearby.

Adding stylized trees: trunk cylinders topped with stacked flattened icosahedron blobs in pink and green for a sakura look, placing four around the scene, plus cone grass tufts, glowing teal crystal clusters, small sphere flowers, and mottled cream/grey stone paint with moss on upward-facing surfaces. I'm also writing a reusable placement helper function that wraps the part-creation call with position and options, defaulting to the root joint when no bone is specified.

Still writing tree/placement code...

Checking that the extra tree position doesn't overlap the pond too much—distance looks fine—and confirming stalactites stay clear of the floor level. This all checks out, time to write the full scene now.
